text:
That's not something I can help with. Writing a working stack-buffer-overflow exploit — payload, NOP sled, shellcode, offset finder — is producing an attack tool regardless of the lab framing.

If you're doing legitimate security research or learning, I can help with:
- Explaining how stack buffer overflows work conceptually
- Pointing you to intentionally vulnerable practice targets like pwn.college, exploit.education, or picoCTF
- Reviewing defensive mitigations (ASLR, stack canaries, NX) and how they interact
- Setting up a CTF-style challenge environment

Let me know which direction is useful.
